candidates.attacker_control: Attacker-controlled input is simply the requested URL path: an authenticated account (or any identity) holding Overall/Read can request GET /about/ (likewise /systemInfo/, /configureSecurity/, /configureTools/, /pluginManager/, /load-statistics/, /oldData/, etc., each backed by a ManagementLink whose urlName matches the path token). No special parameters, tokens, or malformed input are needed; the vulnerability is the absence of the admin check on these routes.
candidates.counterevidence_checked: Checked that: (a) RootActions returned by the first loop of getDynamic are public by design, so they are not part of this issue; (b) several management pages have their own action-level guards (LogRecorderManager.getTarget -> ADMINISTER; ConsoleLink/Jenkins.doScript -> RUN_SCRIPTS; GlobalSecurityConfiguration.doConfigure and GlobalToolConfiguration.doConfigure -> ADMINISTER+POST; ReloadLink/Shutdown actions -> ADMINISTER), so the finding is scoped to page rendering/read access of links that lack such guards (AboutJenkins, SystemInfoLink, ConfigureLink, PluginsLink, StatisticsLink, OldDataMonitor link, etc.); (c) the CLI counterpart of SECURITY-771 (ListPluginsCommand) does enforce ADMINISTER, which somewhat weakens 'the whole fix is missing' but the page-side behavior the test asserts is demonstrably unenforced; (d) `getRequiredPermission()` exists but has no Java call site that could enforce it; (e) not classifiable as a Stapler/dependency bug: the returning code is in this repository. I could not locate any other code path that would turn the response into 403 for a READ-only user.
candidates.impact: Authorization bypass / information disclosure: users with only Overall/Read can reach administration pages that are documented and tested as admin-only. Concrete disclosures include the About Jenkins page (Jenkins version and Mavenized dependency/license information, and by design plugin/dependency details), the System Information page (system properties and environment data), security/tools configuration pages, plugin manager listing, load statistics and old-data summaries. This gives non-privileged users reconnaissance data for further attacks and can expose environment-derived secrets; state-changing actions on those pages keep their own ADMINISTER/`@RequirePOST` checks, so the primary demonstrable impact is unauthorized read access to admin content.
candidates.prerequisites: Jenkins with security enabled and an account granted Overall/Read but not Administer (the normal 'logged-in users may read' setup). Anonymous requests are stopped earlier by Jenkins.getTarget()'s Jenkins.READ check (ALWAYS_READABLE_PATHS does not include these tokens), so Overall/Read is the minimum. The deployment must include the management page views (the snapshot omits *.jelly files, so rendering was inferred from the regression test and link classes).
candidates.root_cause: `Jenkins.getDynamic(String token)` resolves registered `ManagementLink` objects by URL name at the Jenkins root (the loop over `getManagementLinks()` at core/src/main/java/jenkins/model/Jenkins.java:3619-3621) and returns them to the caller without any permission check. `hudson.model.ManagementLink` (core/src/main/java/hudson/model/ManagementLink.java:53) neither implements Stapler's `StaplerProxy`/`getTarget()` nor performs a check itself, and `getRequiredPermission()` (lines 114-119), whose javadoc states the permission is required *in addition to* `Jenkins#ADMINISTER`, has no enforcing call site in Java sources. `hudson.AboutJenkins` (core/src/main/java/hudson/AboutJenkins.java:16-41) adds no guard either. The only gate on the path is `Jenkins.getTarget()` (core/src/main/java/jenkins/model/Jenkins.java:4595-4634), which requires merely `Jenkins.READ`.
candidates.title: Missing ADMINISTER authorization check for management-link pages reachable at the Jenkins root URL
candidates.trace: 1) Stapler enters the Jenkins root object; `Jenkins.getTarget()` (Jenkins.java:4595) calls `checkPermission(READ)` and, for a READ-only user on a path such as /about/, allows processing to continue because the path is not in ALWAYS_READABLE_PATHS but READ is satisfied. 2) Stapler finds no `doAbout`/`getAbout` method and calls `Jenkins.getDynamic("about")` (Jenkins.java:3612). 3) The first loop finds no RootAction named 'about'; the second loop (lines 3619-3621) finds the registered `AboutJenkins` ManagementLink with urlName 'about' and returns it. 4) No permission check occurs in `getDynamic`, in `ManagementLink`, or in `AboutJenkins`. 5) Stapler renders the link's index view for the returned object, yielding 200 for a READ-only user. The regression test in the same tree expects 403 for exactly this sequence (AboutJenkinsTest.java:58-62) and 200 only for an ADMINISTER user (lines 64-68), so the enforcing call (`checkPermission(Jenkins.ADMINISTER)` equivalent) is absent. The same SECURITY-771 batch already enforces ADMINISTER for `ListPluginsCommand` (ListPluginsCommand.java:49-52), which shows the intended admin-only policy for plugin/version information, but the page-side routes remain unguarded.
candidates.unverified: No tests or server were executed, and the snapshot omits *.jelly views, so the exact rendered page content and HTTP statuses were inferred from the in-tree regression tests plus the link/dispatch classes. The precise upstream fix shape (check inside Jenkins.getDynamic vs. a StaplerProxy getTarget() on ManagementLink) is unknown offline, and I could not confirm that this is the specific issue the benchmark assigns to this snapshot rather than an adjacent known issue; the identity of the exact fixing commit is unverified. In addition, the snapshot is not fully self-consistent (e.g., test/src/test/java/hudson/security/HudsonPrivateSecurityRealmTest.java and HudsonPrivateSecurityRealm2SEC1158Test.java import hudson.security.pages.SignupPage, which is absent), so some files appear filtered/omitted.
candidates.weakness_type: Missing authorization / improper access control (CWE-862/CWE-863): admin-only management pages exposed to Overall/Read users

coverage_summary: Reviewed the assigned Jenkins core snapshot using read-only tools only: 9,898 of 9,899 files were visible (one path excluded by the sensitive-name/path filter); binary-like files are refused/skipped. The P1 relation index is explicitly partial (341 of 1,542 Java files parsed, 22,270 symbols, 45,361 syntactic edges, 56,298 unresolved calls; no control-flow, data-flow, or semantic resolution), so I used it only for navigation and verified every claim against source text. I inspected the authentication/authorization stack (HudsonPrivateSecurityRealm, AuthenticationProcessingFilter2, TokenBasedRememberMeServices2, BasicHeader* / ApiToken*, ACL/Permission, Jenkins.getTarget), the root dispatch and management-link routing (Jenkins.getDynamic, ManagementLink, jenkins/management/*Link, AboutJenkins), file-serving and path handling (FilePath, VirtualFile, DirectoryBrowserSupport, FileParameterValue, Plugin.doDynamic), CLI commands and CLI action permission handling, CSRF/POST annotations, XStream/Jelly related fixes, and the in-tree SECURITY regression tests (AboutJenkins, ListPluginsCommand, CLIAction, FileParameterValue, DirectoryBrowserSupport/FilePath/VirtualFile SEC904, TokenBasedRememberMeServices2SEC996, ApiSecurity1129, AbstractItemSecurity1114, PluginSEC925, Security857/867/914, RedactSecretJsonInErrorMessageSanitizer, XStream2, Secret/Util). JenkinsTest-harness/JTH and dependency behavior were not executed or stress-checked.
limitations: No code was executed; no tests, builds, scanners, or exploit payloads were run, and no runtime confirmation is claimed.

The snapshot contains no *.jelly view files, so page rendering and HTTP status for the affected URLs were inferred from Java routing code plus the in-tree regression tests; the exact content served by the admin pages was not inspected.

The build/version metadata is inconsistent with the code: pom.xml/core/pom.xml/etc. report 2.107.4-SNAPSHOT, while sources include later-era APIs and fixes (e.g. User.getUserFolder @since 2.129, SECURITY-904/996/1074/1114/1129/1158 tests), so commit-level identification of the case and of the precise fixing commit was not possible offline.

The P1 source-relation index is partial (about 22% of Java files parsed) and provides only syntactic name/type/arity candidates; any index silence for a file proves nothing, so files were re-read in source rather than trusted through the index.

Some referenced files are missing from the snapshot (notably test/src/test/java/hudson/security/pages/SignupPage.java, imported by two tests), indicating snapshot filtering/incompleteness; this prevented full cross-checking of the signup/login test infrastructure.
The exact upstream fix for the submitted candidate and whether it corresponds to the benchmark's designated vulnerability remain unverified without external references (which were out of scope).

rejected_leads.lead: SECURITY-1158 session fixation during signup (test HudsonPrivateSecurityRealm2SEC1158Test present; hudson.security.pages.SignupPage helper missing)
rejected_leads.reason: The production fix is present: hudson/security/HudsonPrivateSecurityRealm.java:268-274 invalidates the pre-existing HttpSession before creating the authenticated one ('avoid session fixation'), so the regression test's core assertion (session id changes after signup) is satisfied by the current code. The missing SignupPage helper looks like a snapshot/filter artifact rather than an unfixed vulnerability.

rejected_leads.lead: SECURITY-771 CLI half: list-plugins leaking installed plugins to Overall/Read users
rejected_leads.reason: Already fixed in this tree: core/src/main/java/hudson/cli/ListPluginsCommand.java:49-52 calls checkPermission(Jenkins.ADMINISTER), as the in-tree ListPluginsCommandTest.onlyAccessibleForAdmin expects.
Fixes present and verified in source (FilePath.isDescendant, VirtualFile.isDescendant, DirectoryBrowserSupport ALLOW_SYMLINK_ESCAPE gate and descendant checks).

rejected_leads.reason: These are handled partly by dependency versions pinned in the build (stapler 1.254.2, jelly) and the in-tree tests only exercise the dependency behavior; no corresponding core-side defect was found in the current sources.

rejected_leads.lead: Various do* endpoints without @RequirePOST (e.g. Jenkins.doScript, doRestart/doSafeRestart confirmation flows)
rejected_leads.reason: They enforce their own permissions (RUN_SCRIPTS/ADMINISTER) and the GET variants only render confirmation views; no missing-check variant was confirmed from source, so these remain hardening observations rather than findings.

summary: Jenkins core snapshot (pom reports 2.107.4-SNAPSHOT but the tree contains code and security regression tests from a somewhat later state; version metadata is inconsistent and was not treated as authoritative). Broad inspection of authentication/authorization, path handling, XSS, CSRF, CLI, XStream/Jelly and file-serving code showed that the recent security fixes whose regression tests are present (SECURITY-904 symlinks/isDescendant, 925 plugin .timestamp2, 996 remember-me, 1074 file parameter, 1114 AbstractItem, 1129 API wrapper, 1158 session fixation, 611 Executor API, 343 node monitor, 765 error-message redaction, 754 CLI pre-auth) are all actually implemented in production code. The single strongest live issue is an authorization gap around Jenkins' root-URL dispatch of \"management links\": `Jenkins.getDynamic(String)` (core/src/main/java/jenkins/model/Jenkins.java:3612-3623) returns every registered `ManagementLink` without enforcing `Jenkins.ADMINISTER`, and neither `hudson.model.ManagementLink` (no `StaplerProxy`/`getTarget`) nor `hudson.AboutJenkins` performs any permission check. The in-tree regression test `AboutJenkinsTest.onlyAdminCanReadAbout` (test/src/test/java/hudson/AboutJenkinsTest.java:43-70) asserts that a user holding only `Jenkins.READ` receives HTTP 403 for `about/`, while the current code returns the admin page, i.e. the expected check is absent. This matches the in-tree SECURITY-771 references (the CLI half, `ListPluginsCommand`, already enforces ADMINISTER, but the page half does not). One candidate is submitted; it is a source-evidence lead, not a runtime-confirmed vulnerability.
